title.narrative: TF w EBRD on municipal environmental infrastructure

description.narrative:
Bosnia and Herzegovina continues to face many challenges within the fields of municipal infrastructure improvement and adapting to climate change. There are great needs for improved municipal services in the areas of water supply, wastewater treatment, solid waste management, municipal district heating, urban transport and energy efficiency in buildings. To address this issue the Sweden and EBRD have decided to establish the Trust Fund for Bosna and Hercegovina to co-finance municipal environmental infrastructure projects in the country.
The proposed Programme is designed to facilitate consolidated cooperation between Sweden and EBRD to provide support to the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to implement municipal environmental and climate projects. The overall objective of the Programme is to promote the sustainable use of natural resources, protection of the environment and to promote sustainable public services in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The Programme aims to achieve sustainable investments in area of water&waste water, waste management, energy efficiency, district heating and urban transport, resulting in decrease of environmental pollution and contributing to fulfilling EU requirements in area of environment. This includes ensuring that utilities move towards higher quality and reliability of services, as part of the EU-integration process.
The proposed Programme would include two separate components: Investment Grant component - Co-financing investment grants as part of the overall investment package. Investment grants provided under the contribution will help to address affordability and poverty issues allowing time for full cost recovery principles to be introduced gradually. Technical Cooperation component which should help to achieve targeted reforms or promote policy dialogue. TC is used both for project development ahead of project signing and increasingly for project implementation and transition impact related activities post-signing.
Each project to be supported through the TF will have clear activity/output and outcome objectives and will be assessed/approved by Sweden in no-objection procedure.

Bosnien och Hercegovina har fortsatt stora utmaningar vad gäller att förbättra och anpassa den kommunala infrastrukturen i relation till klimatförändringar. Det finns därför ett stort behov för förbättringar avseende kommunala tjänster inom områden som rör vattenförsörjning, hantering av avloppsvatten, avfallshantering, kommunal fjärrvärme, stadstransport och energieffektivisering av byggnader. Som ett led i hanteringen av dessa problem, har ett förslag om en fond för finansiering av kommunala infrastrukturprojekt inom miljöområdet tagits fram av EBRD.
Det förslagna programmet är utformat med syftet att främja det redan etablerade samarbetet mellan Sverige och EBRD och för att stödja Bosnien och Hercegovinas regering i implementeringen av kommunala miljö- och klimatprojekt. Programmets övergripande målsättning är att främja hållbar användning av naturresurser, skydda miljön och skapa hållbar offentlig förvaltning i Bosnien och Hercegovina.
Programmet eftersträvar specifikt att främja hållbara investeringar inom områden som berör vatten, avloppsvatten, avfallshantering, energieffektivitet, fjärrvärme och stadstransport. Därmed är målet att bidra till minskad förorening av miljön samt att bidra till uppfyllandet av de EU-krav som ställs inom miljöområdet. Inom ramarna för EU-integration eftersträvar programmet också att öka kvaliteten och trovärdigheten av de verktyg som används vid genomförandet av dessa tjänster.
Det föreslagna programmet består av två separata komponenter: Investeringsbidrag: Denna komponent berör, som en del av det övergripande investeringspaketet, samfinansiering, tillsammans med EBRDs lånefinansiering, av investeringar. Investeringarna kommer att bidra till att balansera utmaningen att nå långsiktig lönsamhet med kraven på att lägre inkomstskikt skall ha råd till tjänsterna. Med detta kommer det bli möjligt att gradvis införa förutsättningar för kostnadseffektivitet och återhämtning. Tekniskt stöd: Denna komponent förväntas bidra till att eftersträvade reformer uppnås och till att politisk dialog främjas. Komponenten kommer därmed användas dels för projektutveckling innan projektet signeras och därefter för implementering av projektet samt för övergångs-och effektivitets relaterade aktiviteter.
Samtliga projekt inom av förvaltningsfonden kommer att ha tydliga mål för aktiviteter och resultat. Dessa kommer att bedömas/godkännas av Sverige genom ett s k no-objection-förfarande.

The overall objective of the Programme is to promote the sustainable use of natural resources, protection of the environment and to promote sustainable public services in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This includes ensuring that utilities move towards higher quality and reliability of services, as part of the EU-integration process. The project aims to achieve sustainable investments in area of water&waste water, waste management, energy efficiency, district heating and urban transport, resulting in decrease of environmental pollution and contributing to fulfilling EU requirements in area of environment. The proposed Programme would include two separate components:Investment Grant component - Co-financing investment grants as part of the overall investment package. Investment grants provided under the contribution will help to address affordability and poverty issues allowing time for full cost recovery principles to be introduced gradually. Most typically, the costs involved in meeting EU environmental standards far exceed the capacity of a local utility to borrow. Additionally, investment grants may expand the affordable budget for investment while maintaining the commercial discipline, including financial and operational covenants, associated with the loan. Technical Cooperation component which should help to achieve targeted reforms or promote policy dialogue. TC is used both for project development ahead of project signing and increasingly for project implementation and transition impact related activities post-signing .

Key achievements within SWBIH trust fund are presented below: EPBIH Tuzla Biomass CHP study (for which funding was approved in 2023) aims to gather further experience and knowledge about growing short rotation coppice (SRC) on degraded coal mine areas. This study is meant to provide the Company and the Bank with information allowing them to decide on the types of energy crops that can be grown in the target area with a view of replicating the results to larger areas. This assignment supports the development of the investment project that aims to convert a coalfired thermal power plant unit in Tuzla to a biomass fired combined heat and power plant (CHP), the first such CHP to be built in BiH. The planting took place in November 2023, with a total of 4,100 seedlings planted across both locations. The consultant has been regularly reporting on plantation maintenance and monitoring. Reports shown that the crops of acacia plant are resilient to climate changes. The intention is to use the knowledge gained from establishing the test plantations to replicate the results on a much larger area. It is expected that the assignment will conclude in December 2025 at which time the consultant will provide a final report with an overview of all EPBiH activities on energy crops and SRC test plantations with final recommendations for further activities. During the process of planting some concerns have been raised about the potential environmental impacts of converting to biomass, including deforestation and habitat destruction. Some civil society organizations have expressed skepticism about the project's feasibility. The project was put on hold while these concerns were investigated and due to another related assignment (study) having suffered delays. However, feasibility concerns are being addressed and the EBRD intends to proceed with the Tuzla CHP investment project. Based on updated project information, internal EBRD reapproval is expected during Q2 2025. Banja Luka Water Project is a follow-on investment from Banja Lukas Green City Action Plan (GCAP) which was adopted by the City Assembly in 2020. The objective of Banja Luka Water Phase I and Phase II is to improve services in the water resources sector in Banja Luka, which will ensure the connecting technical preconditions from the central water supply system are in place. The project will result in the reduction of water losses, improved operational efficiency and improved quality of services for customers, whilst also benefiting the environment. Through this bilateral intervention Sweden provided technical assistance (TA) for the supervision of the construction and installation works for the second phase of the project. The consultant continues to assist the City during the implementation of the project. The activities are progressing at a satisfactory level alongside the construction works which are close to completion. TA related to financial and operational development of Water Utility, financed through a reginal envelope, is progressing with delays caused by the limited capacity of the City to provide timely responses and feedback to the consultant. Completion of the assignment is expected with the completion of Phase II i.e. by end of September 2025. Expected outcomes of this intervention include (i) short term operation and financial improvement (ii) preparation of a Business Plan (iii) recommendations for specific corporate development measures (iv) preparation of a Public Service Contract Zivinice Regional Solid Waste Project provides funds to a specially created company for the construction of an EU compliant sanitary landfill and a recycling yard to service three municipal regions in BiH benefiting a population of nearly 180.000 citizens. The loan was on-lent, through the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH) and the municipalities of Zivinice, Banovici and Kladanj (the Participating Municipalities), to EkoSep (the Company), a regional waste management company established by the Participating Municipalities in the Tuzla Canton in BiH. In addition to EBRDs loan of 5milEUR, Sweden has supported this project with 2,5milEUR investment grant, enabling the realization of key infrastructure components and ensuring the project's viability by covering the financial gap which allowed the project to be fully implemented. The investment project was signed on 20th November 2019. By now, entire construction have been completed as well as the works supervision services. After obtaining electrical connections and completion of access road (which took some 18 months) all necessary use permits were obtained in August 2024. Finally, the landfill is officially opened in April 2025 and started its operations. The newly constructed landfill will introduce mechanical biological treatment of waste, composting, a transfer station, waste sorting, and landfill gas collection and flaring. In addition to the investment grant Sweden also financed technical assistance related to the corporate development and stakeholder participation aiming to help the newly established Eko Sep Company to set up its operations and to make viable arrangements for ownership by the three Participating Municipalities. This is important as to enable long term sustainability of the overall Project of the Regional Waste Management Center. The assignment is expected to be completed in April 2025.
